classification_policy.evidence_line_numbers: One-based inclusive lines in the exact repository artifact identified by SHA-256. SQL is redacted; original-definition hashes are separate.

role_taxonomy.transactional_state: Stores mutable business-operation quantities, statuses or execution bookkeeping.
role_taxonomy.configuration: Stores parameters, definitions or rules that can govern behavior; values and activation were not inspected.
role_taxonomy.master_reference: Stores reusable identities and descriptive attributes referenced across operations.
role_taxonomy.execution_worklist: Represents warehouse instruction ordering, assignment and execution state; not the generic vendor process queue.
role_taxonomy.reporting_read_model: Projects or aggregates stored data for reading; does not imply materialization or measured workload.
role_taxonomy.presentation_metadata: Stores screen/control definitions, binding properties and display settings.
role_taxonomy.presentation_adapter: Builds result shapes or selections consumed by a user interface or print-selection flow.
role_taxonomy.orchestration: Coordinates conditional database calls or multiple implementation steps; caller transactions remain separate.
role_taxonomy.transactional_mutation: Contains explicit persistent INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE behavior affecting operational state.
role_taxonomy.integration_staging: Stores interface-shaped payloads and processing indicators; direction, transport and delivery need additional evidence.
role_taxonomy.audit_history: Stores events, changes or errors; completeness, retention and immutability are not established.
role_taxonomy.workflow_selection: Builds selection logic for executable warehouse work; not necessarily read-only.
role_taxonomy.utility_transform: Transforms input into derived values or structured parameters.
role_taxonomy.event_handler: Defines trigger behavior for a declared DML event; actual execution was not tested.
role_taxonomy.compatibility_declaration: Retains a procedure signature with no executable body in the captured source; no caller compatibility or invocation is established.
role_taxonomy.paired_structural_record: Has columns compared with a separately identified record shape; pairing does not establish a copy, archive or retention process.
role_taxonomy.structural_copy: Has a matching captured column shape; the label does not establish copying provenance, timing, contents or use.
role_taxonomy.activity_measurement: Provides fields for activity quantities, intervals or costs; formulas, units and actual measured events require separate evidence.
role_taxonomy.request_record: Provides an identified request record and associated fields; processing, payload grammar and retry behavior remain unestablished.
role_taxonomy.authorization_metadata: Represents access associations or permission metadata; actual authorization enforcement is not established by the schema.
role_taxonomy.annotation_data: Stores comments or annotations associated with identifiers; generic identifiers do not establish validated business-object relationships.
role_taxonomy.configuration_payload: Represents configuration-shaped values; their effective use, precedence and execution are not established.
role_taxonomy.staging_payload: Provides an intermediate payload shape; a conversion, import or production-consumer lifecycle requires separate evidence.
role_taxonomy.master_data: Provides reusable entity identities and descriptive fields; current authority, inheritance and consumer behavior require separate evidence.
role_taxonomy.document_metadata: Stores document references or related status fields; document existence, accessibility and upload completion are not established.
role_taxonomy.payload_shape: Provides a structurally described payload without sufficient evidence of a producer, consumer or authoritative operational role.
role_taxonomy.retained_record_shape: Provides a record shape with historical or deleted-state associations; names and fields do not prove events, retention completeness or recoverability.
role_taxonomy.message_payload: Provides message content and related status fields; transmission, acknowledgment, retry and delivery guarantees are not established.
role_taxonomy.request_state: Stores request identity, status or timestamps; stored values do not establish processor behavior or physical outcomes.
role_taxonomy.activity_history: Provides activity record fields; completeness, chronology, duration calculations and actual completed work remain unestablished.
role_taxonomy.content_storage: Stores text or content segments; reconstruction, ordering, encoding and completeness require caller evidence.
role_taxonomy.configuration_state: Provides state used to represent settings or counters; effective values, atomic changes and validation require separate evidence.
role_taxonomy.version_metadata: Stores version or patch provenance fields; this does not establish the installed version of every component.
role_taxonomy.measurement_storage: Provides instrumentation measurement fields; observed values, instrumentation boundaries and whole-process timing are not established.
role_taxonomy.authorization_payload_shape: Provides an authorization-shaped payload without established active use or enforcement.
role_taxonomy.integrity_metadata: Stores hash or integrity-related fields; algorithms, trusted provenance and verification enforcement require separate evidence.
role_taxonomy.metadata_workspace_shape: Provides a metadata-oriented record shape; temporary names do not establish session scope, consumers or cleanup behavior.
role_taxonomy.association_payload_shape: Provides identifiers that can represent associations; valid relationships and operational effects require separate evidence.
role_taxonomy.interface_payload: Provides interface-oriented fields; transport direction, processing, delivery and acknowledgment remain separate claims.
role_taxonomy.activity_state: Stores activity-related state such as timestamps; current presence, authentication and attendance are not established.
role_taxonomy.identity_metadata: Stores user or identity-related attributes; authentication mechanisms and effective privileges require separate evidence.

records.purpose: Perform a maintenance runbook that rewrites archive/filter/scheduled-job configuration and can immediately truncate or delete retained history tables. It is a mutating operational routine, not a read-only archive report.

functional_roles.rationale: Initialize fixed preference/type groups and a four-entry nonproduction server-name list; choose environment branches using @@SERVERNAME. Initialize history-day constants 7, 30, 90, 180 and 372, delete-loop limit 10 and per-delete TOP limit 500000. These are implementation values, not recommended retention policy. Reclassify selected system-created archive and generic configuration records using process-stamp checks and exclusion lists. Capture a custom-preference exclusion set, normalize USER_DEF fields with environment-specific override handling, and replace selected archive process identifiers. Remove two specifically selected archive preferences and associated filter records. Allocate a system-config numeric key beginning at 5000 using an observed gap or maximum-plus-one fallback, then insert a fixed runbook-related system setting or update the existing setting key. cFilterDelete removes filters and preferences for eligible discovered tables/type records when the applicable environment override is absent. Later updates derive USER_DEF5/ACTIVE/RUN_BY_DEFAULT, USER_DEF6/SAVE_DATA and USER_DEF7/DAYS_HIST with special type groups, exclusions and environment branches. cArchiveCreate enumerates eligible base tables plus synthesized process/transaction history type names and inserts missing archive preferences. Four explicitly added tables are LABEL_PRINT_REQUEST, SSRS_PRINTING_REQUEST, UPLOAD_LOCATION_INVENTORY_ATTRIBUTES and UPLOAD_SERIAL_NUMBER. Parent archive identifiers and dynamic handler identifiers are stored as metadata; those handlers are not invoked by this body. cFilterCreate deletes and rebuilds filter header/detail/statement rows for selected preferences. It stores dynamic filter SELECT text for WORK_ORDER_HEADER and WORK_INSTRUCTION condition tests, LAUNCH_STATISTICS closed tests, and PROCESS_HISTORY/TRANSACTION_HISTORY type tests. It then attaches DATA_FILTER. These filter texts are persisted here rather than executed here. When DeleteLoopLimit is positive, cArchiveTruncate selects child archive tables whose parent preference has saving disabled, active enabled and default-run enabled, plus special process/transaction archive cases when no corresponding type preference requests saving. A metadata row-count existence test narrows targets; each non-null target is immediately TRUNCATE TABLE through QUOTENAME. There is no row/batch cap on a selected truncate. cArchiveDelete selects eligible archive preferences with saving disabled and active/default-run enabled. For each non-null target and positive DAYS_HIST, it constructs an age-based delete: DATE_TIME_STAMP <= CONVERT(DATE, GETUTCDATE()-DAYS_HIST), TOP 500000 ordered by DATE_TIME_STAMP, repeated ten times after one initial existence test. Two subsequent cHistDelete passes target AR_PROCESS_HISTORY and AR_TRANSACTION_HISTORY by configured type with saving disabled and active/default-run enabled. These type-specific deletes have no age predicate and no ORDER BY; they perform TOP 500000 up to ten iterations per cursor row. The same underlying table can be visited through more than one preference. Finally update scheduled-job activation/next-run metadata differently for the fixed environment groups, clear selected PARAMETER_DATA, and adjust active interval jobs with frequency below five minutes by adding five minutes to NEXT_RUN_DATE_TIME and setting minimum frequency five, subject to the stated USER_DEF6 exclusion. No scheduler is invoked here. UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE ARCHIVE_PREFERENCES; UPDATE GENERIC_CONFIG_DETAIL; INSERT/UPDATE SYSTEM_CONFIG_DETAIL. DELETE/INSERT FILTER_CONFIG_HEADER, FILTER_CONFIG_DETAIL and FILTER_STATEMENT; UPDATE SCHEDULED_JOBS. Dynamic TRUNCATE TABLE on selected archive table names; dynamic DELETE CTE on age-qualified selected tables and type-qualified AR_PROCESS_HISTORY/AR_TRANSACTION_HISTORY. Local table-variable inserts and cursor state only in addition to the above persistent effects. sp_executesql for each eligible truncate, age-delete, process-history delete and transaction-history delete. No other stored-procedure call is present. Reading DYNAMIC_CALLING_DETAIL and storing ARCHIVE_PROCESS does not execute that handler.

records.purpose: Queue and execute index/statistics maintenance with optional persistent logging.

functional_roles.rationale: Privately verified operations index/statistics/all and modes smart/dummy; invalid non-NULL mode resets smart, NULL mode remainsNULL. Invalid/NULL operation prints help but does not return: it can still create AzureSQLMaintenanceLog even LogToTable=0, and optional logging/retention still runs. Index discovery uses LIMITED physical stats and index types1/2; smart queues page_count>40 and fragmentation>=5, reorganizing strictly>5 and<30, so exactly5 rebuilds. Dummy means broad real maintenance, not dry-run; OR dummy bypasses preceding queue predicates. Partition rows can produce repeated whole-index commands because partition_number is not inserted into command. Online-support heuristic checks index_id>=1000 only within prefiltered temp data. Statistics selects non-sys rows with modifications or dummy and forms rows/modification info, which can divide by zero. Unordered DELETE TOP1 queue executes each command inside TRY/CATCH, optionally logs command/status using SCOPE_IDENTITY, then continues after errors. Keeps three most recent distinct operation times when logging. Unsuffixed payload uses plain REORGANIZE, REBUILD MAXDOP=1 with ONLINE ON/OFF choice, and UPDATE STATISTICS WITH FULLSCAN.

functional_roles.rationale: Private fragment inspection confirms dynamic ALTER TABLE. COLUMNPROPERTY IsComputed NULL is treated as absent column and selects ADD with optional default/identity; existing column selects ALTER COLUMN, suppresses those clauses and drops detected default first. Nullable flagY uses NULL, elseNOT NULL. Check-constraint modeY forces nullable column, then if fixed constructed constraint name absent adds WITH NOCHECK CHECK(column IS NOT NULL). In normal modeN an existing dropped default is re-added using caller value or DEFAULT NULL; existing column without prior default does not gain one through this path. Recursively applies to existing AR_/IA_ prefixed tables and special RECEIPT_CONTAINER -> DELETED_RECEIPT_CONTAINER; special recursion omits check-mode argument and uses defaultN. Finally check-modeY with non-NULL default performs unfiltered UPDATE table SET column=default, overwriting existing values. Unquoted names/type/default syntax concatenated into nvarchar500 statement; no allowlist or recursion limit.

Item presence chooses item/company or item-class paths; unordered TOP 1 item template lookups and unordered variable assignment can select ambiguous candidates. A found sequence below one returns -1; otherwise return ISNULL(MAX(existing preceding unit sequence),0)+1. A NULL template sequence takes the ELSE path and returns 1 because the preceding comparison finds no rows. No unit row is inserted.
